bmt-2019-team-01.title: Longest chord
bmt-2019-team-01.body:
$\left|e^{2\pi ik/2019}-1\right|$ is the distance on the unit circle from $1$ to the point at angle $\frac{2\pi k}{2019}$. It is maximal when that point is as close as possible to $-1$, i.e. $\frac k{2019}$ is as close as possible to $\frac12$. Since $2019$ is odd, the best integers are $k=1009$ and $k=1010$ (both at distance $\frac1{2\cdot2019}$ from $\frac12$ in units of a turn). The larger is $1010$.

**Answer: 1010**

bmt-2019-team-03.title: Circular segment
bmt-2019-team-03.body:
The water level is horizontal, so the water fills the part of the circular cross-section (radius $5$) below height $\frac{15}2$; the dry part is a cap of height $10-\frac{15}2=\frac52$. The chord is at distance $5-\frac52=\frac52$ from the centre, so the half-angle $\alpha$ satisfies $\cos\alpha=\frac12$, $\alpha=60^\circ$, and the cap's central angle is $120^\circ$.

Cap area $=$ sector $-$ triangle $=\frac13\cdot25\pi-\frac12\cdot25\sin120^\circ=\frac{25\pi}3-\frac{25\sqrt3}4$. The water's cross-section is $25\pi$ minus this: $\frac{50\pi}3+\frac{25\sqrt3}4$. The height of the cylinder is $1$, so the volume is the same number.

**Answer: $\frac{50\pi}3+\frac{25\sqrt3}4$**

bmt-2019-team-04.title: Multiset permutations
bmt-2019-team-04.body:
CATALYSIS has $9$ letters with A and S repeated twice: $C=\frac{9!}{2!2!}$. TRANSPORT has $9$ letters with T and R twice: $T=\frac{9!}{2!2!}=C$. STRUCTURE has $9$ letters with T, R, U each twice: $S=\frac{9!}{2!2!2!}$. MOTION has $6$ letters with O twice: $M=\frac{6!}{2!}=360$.

So $C-T=0$ and $\frac SM=\frac{9!/8}{360}=\frac{45360}{360}=126$.

**Answer: 126**

bmt-2019-team-05.title: Round the real solution
bmt-2019-team-05.body:
Solve $21a-19b=2019$, $19b+21a=470$: adding gives $42a=2489$ ($a\approx59.2$), subtracting gives $38b=-1549$ ($b\approx-40.8$). The points $(21a-19b,\,21a+19b)=a\,(21,21)+b\,(-19,19)$ form a lattice generated by two perpendicular vectors, so the nearest lattice point to the target is found by rounding each coordinate $(a,b)\approx(59.27,-40.76)$: $a=59$, $b=-41$. This gives $(2018,460)$, at distance $\sqrt{1^2+10^2}=\sqrt{101}$.

**Answer: $\sqrt{101}$**

bmt-2019-team-06.title: Divisibility
bmt-2019-team-06.body:
Teams have exactly three people and $2019=3\cdot673$ is divisible by $3$, so the number of people not on a team is always a multiple of $3$. It can never be exactly $1$, so the probability is $0$.

**Answer: 0**

bmt-2019-team-07.title: Case on b
bmt-2019-team-07.body:
We need $b^8+m^4+t^2=2018$. Since $3^8>2018$, $|b|\le2$. Mod $4$, even powers are $0$ or $1$ and $2018\equiv2$, so exactly two of $b,m,t$ are odd.

- $b=0$: need $m^4+t^2=2018$ with $m,t$ odd; $|m|\in\{1,3,5\}$ gives $2017,1937,1393$, none a square.
- $b=\pm1$: need $m^4+t^2=2017$ with $m,t$ of opposite parity. $m=\pm3$ gives $2017-81=1936=44^2$, so $t=\pm44$: $2\cdot2\cdot2=8$ triples (signs of $b$, $m$, $t$). No other $m$ works.
- $b=\pm2$: need $m^4+t^2=2018-256=1762$ with $m,t$ odd; $m=\pm3$ gives $1681=41^2$: another $8$ triples.

Total $16$ (a computer check confirms $16$).

**Answer: 16**

bmt-2019-team-08.title: Which k are allowed
bmt-2019-team-08.body:
If $x^2-5x+k$ has rational roots they are integers $r$ and $5-r$ (monic integer polynomial), so $k=r(5-r)$ with $r\ne0,5$. The distinct values are $4,6$ (from $r=1,4$ and $r=2,3$) and $-6,-14,-24,\dots$ (from $r=6,7,8,\dots$, equivalently $r=-1,-2,\dots$). Every value is used at most once.

To make the sum as small as possible, use every negative value and omit the positive values $4,6$: the sum is $\sum_{r\ge6}\frac1{r(5-r)}=-\frac15\sum_{r\ge6}\left(\frac1{r-5}-\frac1r\right)=-\frac15\left(1+\frac12+\frac13+\frac14+\frac15\right)=-\frac15\cdot\frac{137}{60}$, using a telescoping sum. Then $\frac15\cdot\left(-\frac{137}{300}\right)=-\frac{137}{1500}$.

**Answer: $-\frac{137}{1500}$**

bmt-2019-team-09.title: Lower bound and construction
bmt-2019-team-09.body:
Lower bound: the interior, three faces meeting at a vertex, and that vertex are pairwise adjacent (the three faces pairwise share an edge), so $5$ colours are needed.

Upper bound: use one colour for the interior and one for all vertices (vertices are not adjacent to each other, and each is adjacent only to edges, faces and the interior). For each of the three axes make one colour class consisting of the two opposite faces perpendicular to that axis together with the four edges parallel to that axis. Inside a class the faces are opposite (no shared edge), the four edges are pairwise disjoint (no shared vertex), and the edges parallel to the axis are not edges of the two faces perpendicular to it, so there is no adjacency. This uses $3+1+1=5$ colours (a computer search also confirms that $4$ colours are impossible).

**Answer: 5**

bmt-2019-team-10.title: Wilson-type argument
bmt-2019-team-10.body:
$2019=3\cdot673$ with $673$ prime. Mod $673$: each nonzero residue $r$ mod $673$ occurs among $r,\,r+673,\,r+1346$, exactly one of which is a multiple of $3$, so the product $P$ of the units below $2019$ contains each residue $1,\dots,672$ exactly twice and $P\equiv(672!)^2\equiv(-1)^2=1\pmod{673}$ by Wilson's theorem. Mod $3$: there are $673$ numbers $\equiv1$ and $672$ numbers $\equiv2$ among them, so $P\equiv1^{673}\cdot2^{672}=4^{336}\equiv1\pmod3$. By the Chinese remainder theorem $P\equiv1\pmod{2019}$.

(Alternatively: the unit group mod $2019$ is $\mathbb Z_2\times\mathbb Z_{672}$, which has more than one element of order $2$, so the product of all its elements is the identity.)

**Answer: 1**

bmt-2019-team-11.title: Symmetry between the two matchups
bmt-2019-team-11.body:
For players $a$ and $b$, the sequence of calls when $a$ bats against $b$ is the same as when $b$ bats against $a$: pitch by pitch, a bit pair $(0,0)$ is a ball, $(1,1)$ a hit and $(0,1)$ or $(1,0)$ a strike, which is symmetric in the two players. Hence both plate appearances have the same result. Every plate appearance ends (within six pitches, either a hit occurs or we have $s+b=6$ with $s\ge3$ or $b\ge4$).

If the result is a hit, $a$ scores a point as a batter and $b$ scores one as a batter in the other game; if it is an out, $a$ scores as a pitcher and $b$ scores as a pitcher in the other game. Either way each of the two players gains exactly one point from the pair of games. So every player gets exactly $1$ point from each of the $63$ opponents: every score is $63$, so the highest is $63$.

**Answer: 63**

bmt-2019-team-12.title: Small cases and doubling
bmt-2019-team-12.body:
Shooting when $n$ people remain turns the shooter into the last player of an $(n-1)$-person game, so only the neighbour on the left is ever shot. For $n=1$ the single player wins, for $n=2$ player $1$ wins; for $n=3$ the first player loses either way, so he shoots and player $3$ wins; for $n=4$ player $1$ shoots and becomes the last player of a $3$-person game, so player $1$ wins. In general, if player $k\ne n$ wins the $n$-person game then player $k+2$ wins the $(n+1)$-person game, and if player $n$ wins then player $1$ wins the next game.

Thus person $1$ wins whenever $n$ is a power of $2$, person $n$ wins when $n=2^k-1$, and for $2^k\le n<2^{k+1}$ the winner is $2n-2^{k+1}+1$. (A direct computer simulation of the rules confirms this formula for every $n<160$.) For $n=2019$ ($2^{10}\le n<2^{11}$): $2\cdot2019-2048+1=1991$.

**Answer: 1991**

bmt-2019-team-13.title: Triangle BPC
bmt-2019-team-13.body:
The area of $ABC$ is $84$ (Heron), its circumradius is $R=\frac{13\cdot14\cdot15}{4\cdot84}=\frac{65}8$. $AP$ bisects $\angle A$, so $P$ is the midpoint of arc $BC$ not containing $A$, on the perpendicular bisector of $BC$. The distance from the circumcentre to $BC$ is $\sqrt{R^2-7^2}=\frac{33}8$, so the distance from $P$ to $BC$ is $R-\frac{33}8=4$. Then $[BPC]=\frac12\cdot14\cdot4=28$, and $[ABPC]=84+28=112$.

**Answer: 112**

bmt-2019-team-14.title: Unfold the reflections
bmt-2019-team-14.body:
Reflecting the hexagon instead of the laser, the path becomes a straight line through the hexagonal tiling, ending at the first tiling vertex it meets. All tiling vertices and tile centres together form a triangular lattice of spacing equal to the side length $s$, so $a^2=s^2(x^2+xy+y^2)$ for integers $x,y$; in particular $a^2$ is a number of the form $u^2+uv+v^2$, which is never $2\pmod 4$ and never $2\pmod 3$.

$2019^2+1\equiv2\pmod4$ and $2019^2+2\equiv2\pmod3$ (since $3\mid2019$), so both are impossible. $2019^2+3=4076364=2018^2+2018\cdot2+2^2$ is achievable: take side length $s=2$ and the lattice vector $(1009,1)$ (in units of $s$), norm $1009^2+1009+1=1019091$ and $4\cdot1019091=4076364$. The vector is primitive and its endpoint is a vertex (not a hexagon centre), so the laser reaches that corner without meeting an earlier one.

**Answer: $2019^2+3$**

bmt-2019-team-15.title: Decide which operation is which, then eliminate
bmt-2019-team-15.body:
Name the values $p=$ ⋔, $q=$ ▷, $r=$ ⋏, $s=$ ⊚, $u=$ ϰ, $f=$ ⋗, $g=$ ⋉, $h=$ ♢, $i=$ ⋓, $j=$ □.

Suppose $\eta$ were multiplication and $\gamma$ addition. Then $(j+f)\cdot i=p\cdot i=j$ (using $j\gamma f=p$ and $p\eta i=j$), but also $(j+f)\cdot i=j\cdot i+f\cdot i=f+h=q$ (using $j\eta i=f$, $f\eta i=h$, $f\gamma h=q$). So $j=q$, contradicting that different symbols have different values. Hence $\eta=+$ and $\gamma=\cdot$.

The equations become $p+q=r$, $s u=f$, $g f=r$, $f h=q$, $f+i=h$, $f+g=u$, $j f=p$, $p+i=j$, $j+i=f$. First $f\ne0$ (otherwise $p=jf=0$ and $q=fh=0$ would be equal values for different symbols). Then $r=p+q=jf+fh=f(j+h)$ and $r=gf$ give $g=j+h=j+(f+i)=f+f=2f$ (using $j+i=f$). So $u=f+g=3f$, and $s\cdot3f=f$ gives $s=\frac13$.

**Answer: $\frac13$**
